| Scene description | • Qunguang Plaza, Hongshan District, covers pedestrian shopping space and roadside pavement.<br>• S04-A-01: blue recyclables and black other-waste bins beside a glass entrance do not overflow; ash accumulates in the central silver ashtray.<br>• S04-A-02: a black other-waste bin at a food entrance has an overflowing liner and a little nearby litter.<br>• S04-A-03: an unmarked stainless-steel cylindrical bin beside planting overflows.<br>• S04-A-04: a non-overflowing roadside sorting bin has two tied black bags containing plastic and other waste on the ground.<br>• S04-A-05: a black other-waste bin against a wall overflows with white bags and packaging. Shared bicycles, planters, glass shop doors, and vehicles surround these locations; cleanliness is moderate, with overflow and ground accumulations. |
| Regulatory basis | • Property or shopping-center managers should collect and maintain commercial bins to prevent overflow and accumulation (Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 15).<br>• Stockpiling or discarding waste outside bins is prohibited and may entail correction and fines (Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste, Article 23).<br>• Sorting facilities require clear labels and capacity matched to generation (Implementation Plan for the Municipal Solid Waste Classification System, State Council General Office Document [2017] No. 26, Article 4).<br>• Overflow or accumulation left beyond 24 hours may constitute management neglect, incurring warnings or fines (Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 32).<br>• Ashtrays and dedicated facilities require regular cleaning against ash or material accumulation (Detailed Rules for the Implementation of the Regulations on Public Place Sanitation Management, Article 10).<br>• Commercial pedestrian areas require scheduled inspections and daily removal (Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste, Article 18). |
| Severity | **Moderate.** Five overflowing bins and three ground accumulations are reported across five locations. Pollution is not extensive, but exposed and scattered waste moderately impair pedestrian experience, commercial cleanliness, and urban appearance. |
| Impact assessment | Visible impacts: exposed overflow and ground bags impair pedestrian-area cleanliness; accumulated ash may cause insects or odors. Possible short-term impacts: delays may attract flying insects and rodents, increasing vector risks, complaints, and negative publicity affecting the mall and surroundings. |
| Potential causes | - **Possible cause 1:** excessive collection intervals, indicated by five overflowing bins and exposed bags; verify records and plans.<br>- **Possible cause 2:** insufficient capacity or numbers; two external bags at non-overflowing S04-A-04 may indicate demand beyond capacity. Observe peak pedestrian and waste volumes.<br>- **Possible cause 3:** unclear responsibilities or oversight; unmarked S04-A-03 may be temporary or unmanaged. Review responsibility documents.<br>- **Possible cause 4:** weak sorting awareness, indicated by ash at S04-A-01 and external bags at S04-A-04. Check guidance and education. |
| Long-term effects | If persistent or recurrent, odors and vectors may impair sanitation and health; commercial reputation, satisfaction, and business activity may decline; enforcement pressure, negative governance listings, or media exposure may increase; and continued inaction may incur fines under Article 32 of the Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management or credit sanctions. |
| Recommendations | - **Immediate actions:** empty S04-A-02, S04-A-03, and S04-A-05; remove ground bags; clean ashtrays thoroughly; inspect and replace missing bin labels.<br>- **Long-term measures:** (1) increase collections during midday and evening peaks to ensure daily removal; (2) assess capacity and add or replace bins as needed; (3) inspect and supervise with reporting, response, rectification, and feedback; (4) provide sorting guidance and education in pedestrian areas. |
| Priority | **High.** Concentrated, numerous overflow and accumulation locations in a busy pedestrian shopping area directly impair cleanliness and public experience and pose sanitation risks, requiring prompt action against wider impacts. |
